title: Miliastra business operation ledger record, contractVersion 1
description: The minimum a business ledger row must carry so that an operation can be reconciled without dispatching anything. Field shape only - T06 owns the implementation, the journal layout and the recovery of a crashed instance. The ledger is the only writer of operationId; tools/authoring/author.py remains the bottom-layer truth for the native requestId, and the two are bound once and immutably.

schemaVersion.description: Integer, on persisted records. Distinct from the string contractVersion.

payloadDigest.description: Digest of the business payload as this server canonicalised it, not of what the caller sent.

state.description: The authoritative lifecycle state. reconcileState is derived, never stored as the truth.

dispatchEvidence.description: The named files whose presence moved the state from claimed to dispatched. Empty means claimed. This array is the discriminator, quoted from tools/game-executor/scene_cli.py:685-694.

requestId.description: The bottom-layer requestId once it exists. Bound once; a later attempt must never write a second value here.

owner.description: The single claim holder. Atomic claim, one owner, at most one side effect.

allOf.$comment: OPS-4: dispatched requires evidence. A row may not claim dispatched without naming the file that proved it, and may not omit the array.
claimed means explicitly that no dispatch evidence was found - not that nobody looked. The array must be present and empty, so 'not checked' cannot be written as 'claimed'.
OPS-3: a never-claimed row is the only state from which rejected may be produced.
A terminal state must explain itself.
